items.title: 61529_Maxine Sullivan oral history interview
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...looking in Brian Rust, we also find listed something which isn't in the Bruyninckx... And somebody I read attributes -- oh, it's Rust, excuse me. Brian Rust thinks that they were recorded in the summer of 1941.

ctx.x: I wound up having to record 'St. Louis Blues' for several different outfits too. It got to be a pretty big number. In fact, that was one of the numbers in my repertoire that I had to do when I was doing vaudeville -- one of the four selections; 'Loch Lomond,' 'St. Louis Blues', and any two I could find in-between that were currently popular. But those are the standards.

I should mention that we've been taking most of the discographical material from the Bruyninckx discography. But looking in Brian Rust, we also find listed something which isn't in the Bruyninckx. And that's a session on the 11th of June 1940, also for Columbia, in which two sides were made; 'Mad About The Boy' and 'Under The Greenwood Tree'.
